When trying to calibrate the model, sites where eels are translocated will act
as outliers, diminishing the real effect of dams as eels are found above very
large cumulated heights. 
For that reason the eels found above cumulated height of 150 m and 300 m have
been analysed site by site. 
There can be several reasons why eels might be found there. The first is that
operations of transport have taken place, those might of might not have been
recorded. The second is that cumulated height are wrong. Reasons behing this
are often duplicated dams, dams corresponding to penstock pipes with a lateral
reservoir with the hpp located on the bank of the river but without impact on
the river continuity. Dams recently built or simply planned and reported as
being constructed. And finally, in France, where the dam database is very
detailed, lateral dams often built in the downstream areas that are projected
on the main river. 



```{r check_transport, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE, include=FALSE}
frsppt$transport <- "unknown"
frsppt$transport[frsppt$cs_height_10_p>150 & !is.na(frsppt$cs_height_10_p) & 
				frsppt$densCS>0 & !is.na(frsppt$densCS)]<-"possible"
frsppt$transport[frsppt$cs_height_10_p>300  &
				!is.na(frsppt$cs_height_10_p) & 
				frsppt$densCS>0]<-"sure"
sqldf("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS sudoang.ers_full;")
sqldf("CREATE TABLE sudoang.ers_full as select * from frsppt;")
sqldf("SELECT AddGeometryColumn ('sudoang','ers_full','geom',3035,'POINT',2, false);")
sqldf("UPDATE sudoang.ers_full set geom=join_station_rn.geom FROM
				france.join_station_rn  WHERE join_station_rn.st_id=ers_full.op_id
				and country='FR';")
sqldf("UPDATE sudoang.ers_full set geom=dbeel_station.the_geom FROM
				sudoang.dbeel_station   WHERE dbeel_station.op_id=uuid(ers_full.op_id)
				and ers_full.country in ('PT','SP');")
```

## Problems with projection in the downstream path of large rivers (France)

One of the reasons large cumulated height are sometimes found in France is that
some obstacles are connected to lateral artificial canals or outlets that are
not recorded in the RHT (the theoretical simplified river network used in France Pella et al. (2012)). 
Some of these dams have been attributed the category
of dam (i.e. blocking more than the river bed) which is wrong, in fact those
should be weirs. Since they are often a bit complex in their management, they
don't have a height, and the model of height used to predict uses the river
flow in France. So these "lateral" obstacle are used in the model and some
large rivers, free in their downstream course are attributed obstacles that
don't really exist. For that reason all dams predictions on rivers having a
flow larger than 150 m3/s have been set a height of zero. They are selected by
the following query.

```{sql view_badly_projected, eval=FALSE}
/*
 this view allows to remove dams from the main streams when they are projected on the border
*/
 
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS sudoang.downstream_badly_projected;
create view sudoang.downstream_badly_projected as(
select  o.*,   
rn_rna.seaidsegment, 
  rn_rna.basin, 
  rn_rna.riverwidthm, 
  rn_rna.dis_m3_pyr_riveratlas from dbeel_rivers.join_obstruction_rn d
JOIn dbeel_rivers.rn_rna on rn_rna.idsegment=d.idsegment
JOIN sudoang.view_obstruction o on o.op_id=d.op_id
where dis_m3_pyr_riveratlas>150
and po_obstruction_height is NULL
and op_op_id is NULL
order by dis_m3_pyr_riveratlas);
```
